Binance Intelligence Explained: Binance AI vs. Binance AI Pro vs. Agent OS

2026-10-26

Main Takeaways

  • Binance Intelligence is a lineup of three AI products: Binance AI, an in-app personal assistant for everyday users; Binance AI Pro, a no-code financial agent that turns trading ideas into automated workflows; and Agent OS, a developer platform for connecting external AI agents to Binance’s tools and deep liquidity.

  • What separates them is their main capabilities. Binance AI only ever informs and doesn’t act, AI Pro helps users build automated strategies without code, and Agent OS hands execution to an external agent that a developer connects and grants permissions to.

  • All three products keep the user in charge by design. Permissions, funding limits, isolated sub-accounts, and the ability to revoke access at any time run through every product.

Under the banner of Binance Intelligence, Binance has launched three different AI products in the past few months: Binance AI, Binance AI Pro, and Agent OS. If you’ve found yourself wondering what separates them, or which one actually fits what you’re trying to do, you’re not alone. This guide breaks down what each product does, who it’s built for, and how to choose between them.

What Is Binance Intelligence?

Binance Intelligence is Binance's lineup of three AI products: Binance AI, Binance AI Pro, and Agent OS. Rather than one tool trying to be everything, we’ve given you the ability to pick and choose what suits you best.

  • Binance AI sits inside the app as a 24/7 personal assistant. 

  • Binance AI Pro is a workbench for turning trading ideas into tested, automated workflows.

  • Agent OS gives developers a toolkit to connect their AI agents to Binance trading, market data, wallet, and payment capabilities.

See Which One Fits You

What Is Binance AI?

Binance AI is a personal assistant built into the Binance app that surfaces market context around the assets you hold and the way you use the app. The initial release leans on a handful of features: 

  • Generative UI reshapes the Markets Tab around whatever asset or event you’re looking at, pulling in summaries and analysis from trusted data that are personalized according to your usage and asset holdings. 

  • Market Brief gives a short read on crypto and traditional markets through the day, to read or listen to. 

  • Smart Tool Tips deliver contextual guidance based on where you are in the app and your experience level.

  • Master Trade shows how popular investors are positioned while leaving the decision to invest with you.

Note that Binance AI does not trade for you. It only arranges information around your situation so you can make better informed decisions.

How Does Binance AI Pro Work?

Binance AI Pro lets you describe a trading strategy in plain language, test it in practice mode, and run it as an automated workflow once you approve it, all without writing code. 

Some examples include:

  • Daily market report

  • Dollar-cost averaging plan for Bitcoin

  • Conservative approach for a $1,000 account

With your prompt written out, AI Pro will help plan out your strategy, fill in the gaps, and visualize the logic on a canvas. You can run the strategy in paper trading mode before any real money is involved. Going live needs your explicit approval and a functionality check from Binance AI Pro. 

The functionality check is only a confirmation that the logic executes without error. It is not a verdict on whether your strategy will make money. Each live workflow then runs in its own sub-account, walled off from your main balance. You can pause, adjust, or revoke your workflows from the app at any time. 

AI Pro is available on a free Standard plan that covers the whole path from idea to live trading, using DeepSeek and a monthly 250,000 credit allowance. The Premium plan at 19.99 USDC per month offers a monthly 10,000,000 credit allowance, manual top-ups, and access to frontier models such as ChatGPT and Claude, where available.

What Is Agent OS?

Agent OS is a developer platform that connects external AI agents to Binance capabilities such as trading, market data, wallet, and payments, within user-defined limits. 

The quickest way to connect is through the Binance MCP server. This allows your agent to read market data and trade on your behalf. Other capabilities, such as payments and on-chain activity, require other integrations within the Agent OS toolkit.

For security reasons, all agent permissions are turned off by default except the ability to read the user’s portfolio, balances, transaction history, and market data. Agent OS works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and ChatGPT, as well as self-built agents, and a Skills Hub supplies a curated library of skills so you don’t need to build from scratch.

Agent OS is not an autonomous trading system; an agent can only act on what you allow it to do. Like Binance AI Pro, agents use isolated sub-accounts separate from your main balance.

Which Binance Intelligence Product Should You Use?

If you want to keep making every call while the app explains more, stick to Binance AI. If you’re trying to build an automated trading workflow, try using AI Pro. If you’re building a full-on agent that acts within set limits, consider Agent OS.

Note that you don’t have to limit yourself to one of the three products. You might use Binance AI for a daily read of the market, while an AI Pro workflow handles your strategy in the background.

Final Thoughts

Binance Intelligence puts institutional-grade artificial intelligence in your hands, across crypto, stocks, and tokenized securities. Binance AI explains, AI Pro builds and runs what you approve, and Agent OS opens the door to agents with your permission. Whichever one you pick, you’re always in control. Our suite of AI products can only do as much as you permit them to.

If you’re still not sure where to start, Binance AI is the easiest on-ramp: no setup, no sub-account, just better context on what you already hold. From there, AI Pro and Agent OS are there whenever you’re ready to go further. For a long time, tools like this sat behind trading desks and research teams, reserved for people with the budget and the expertise to use them. Binance Intelligence puts that same caliber of tooling in your hands, and leaves every decision in them too.

Main Takeaways

  • bStocks are tokenized securities, BEP-20 tokens on BNB Smart Chain giving 1:1 price exposure to a real, U.S.-listed stock, held in a regulated custodian account.

  • Users can buy and sell bStocks with USDT 24/7, with zero-fee 1:1 conversion to the underlying share.

  • bStocks do not have voting rights, and dividends auto-reinvest via the Multiplier rather than pay cash. 

Can I Buy Tokenized Stocks with USDT on Binance?

Binance supports buying tokenized securities, known as bStocks, with USDT. There are three ways you can buy bStocks.

  1. Buy bStocks directly on Spot with USDT. Trade bStocks on Binance Spot the same way you would with any other digital asset. The minimum order value is 5 USDT.

  2. Buy the stock, then convert to bStocks 1:1. Buy the underlying stock using USDC, USDT, U, BNB, or USD1, then convert it to the corresponding bStock at a 1:1 rate. The minimum order size is $5.

  3. Buy bStocks using Binance Convert. Convert directly into bStocks with a minimum order size of $0.1.

bStocks trade 24/7, including weekends and holidays. bStocks held in your Binance account can be withdrawn to a compatible external wallet or converted 1:1 to the underlying real share at any time.

Trading bStocks on Spot follows Binance's standard trading fees, which are tiered by VIP level. You can see the current rates on the Binance trading fee page. Direct stock trades (method 2) carry a minimum fee of $0.17, or 5 bps (0.05%) on orders above $340.

Tokenized Stocks vs. Tokenized Securities

While similar, there are slight differences. A tokenized stock is one kind of tokenized security; specifically, one representing a single company's equity. "Tokenized security" is the broader category: any traditional financial instrument (equities, funds, ETFs, bonds) represented on-chain as a token.

Understanding What Binance Is (And Isn’t) Is the Best Defense Against Scams

2026-10-20

Main Takeaways

  • Understanding the true role of Binance and practicing critical thinking are essential defenses against increasingly sophisticated scams and impersonators.

  • Binance empowers users with tools and education for financial freedom but will never provide investment advice or solicit funds.

  • In an age of advanced AI and deepfake technology, maintaining skepticism and verifying information through official channels are crucial for staying safe.

Scammers have grown unnervingly good at pretending to be us. One of the most troubling tactics we see is the deepfake: lifelike, AI-generated impersonations of Binance executives and employees soliciting money on video calls that look and sound real enough to make anyone hesitate. The personas are fabricated, but the sophistication is genuine.

Every day, people are contacted by impersonators using the names, likenesses, and even job titles of Binance staff to solicit investments or financial transactions via WhatsApp, Telegram, and other channels. It’s devastating to see people scammed out of their money, and we feel a deep responsibility to address this directly.

We always try to warn and educate our users that neither Binance nor anyone representing it will ever contact you to offer investment advice or solicit funds. But with fakes becoming so realistic, we understand the fear and confusion many feel. How can we protect ourselves in an age where the truth is so easily manipulated?

One critical defense is understanding what Binance is and isn’t, and practicing critical thinking when interacting online. This clarity can help you recognize a scam the moment it asks you to act.

Is Binance a Financial Advisor? What Binance Does and Doesn’t Do

Binance is not a financial advisor, and it will never tell you where to invest or ask you for funds. A major source of confusion is a fundamental misunderstanding of what Binance stands for. As a global financial platform, Binance has become a household name for millions, synonymous with cryptocurrency, and even broader financial opportunity. 

For some, especially those new to financial services, the perception is that Binance is a one-stop solution for all things finance: a platform, a trusted financial advisor, and even a personal guide to managing money.

But here's the truth.

Binance is committed to empowering users by building the infrastructure for the future of finance. Our mission is to increase financial freedom by providing the tools and resources to explore digital assets and traditional finance in one place. We want to make it easy for you to start your financial journey and protect your funds, while equipping you with the education to make smart, informed decisions.

However, it's important to be crystal clear: Binance is not your financial advisor. We will never tell you where to invest your money, promise guaranteed returns, or ask you for funds. Our approach is all about empowerment: we teach you how to navigate the space, make your own choices, and take control of your financial future.

This principle is at the heart of everything we do, from our leadership team down to the customer support agents who are here to help you with questions. We believe in providing the best tools and resources, but the responsibility for financial decisions lies with you.

Binance is here to support your journey, not make the choices for you. Our platform is your gateway to financial exploration, but ultimately, the power to make decisions rests with you.

How Scammers Use AI and Deepfakes to Impersonate Binance Staff

This brings us back to the danger posed by skilled impersonators. Scammers prey on people's growing interest in investing and digital finance, and the trust they have in Binance, often masquerading as Binance employees or executives to exploit the credibility we've built. With advances in AI and deepfake technology, they can create personas that look and sound real.

Technology alone isn’t what makes these scams work. Scammers succeed by exploiting confusion and misplaced trust. They count on you to believe that Binance employees might contact you with unsolicited advice or "special opportunities." This is why it's vital to remember: no one from Binance will ever tell you how to spend your money or promise you returns.

If you ever receive such a message, pause and ask yourself: Is this person empowering me with knowledge, or are they directing me to act in a specific way? Does this feel like the behavior of a helpful guide, or someone trying to exploit my trust?

When in doubt, reach out to Binance through our official support channels. We're here to help you navigate the future of finance safely, but we rely on you to exercise caution and skepticism when approached online.

How to Protect Yourself From Online Scams

One of the best ways to protect yourself is to cultivate a healthy skepticism toward anything you come across online. Just because something seems convincing doesn't mean it's trustworthy. Technology can fake appearances, but it can't replicate the integrity behind a trusted platform like Binance.

Think of Binance as your compass, not your map. We equip you with the direction and tools to explore the world of finance, but the journey is yours to own. Scammers, on the other hand, are like fake maps – promising shortcuts to success, but leading you straight into traps that result in financial loss.

As AI technology continues to evolve, distinguishing between what's real and what's fake will only get harder. That’s why it's essential to stay grounded in what you know about Binance. Know what we stand for and, just as importantly, what we don’t do. We will never promise you easy profits or solicit funds. Keep these principles in mind, and you'll be better able to spot the difference between real opportunities and dangerous scams.

At Binance, we deeply empathize with those affected by scams. We understand the gravity of losing money to bad actors and the emotional toll it takes. That’s why we're committed to educating our users and ensuring they have the tools to protect themselves.

Remember this: Binance is here to empower you, not direct you.

In an era where seeing is no longer believing, let's rely on knowledge, principles, and critical thinking to guide us. Think of it as building a firewall in your mind – one that makes you much harder to fool. Stay safe, stay informed, and remember: the power to protect yourself lies with you.

Prompt, Test, and Trade with Binance AI Pro

Main Takeaways

  • Describe your idea the way you would explain it to a friend, and Binance AI Pro turns it into an automated workflow.

  • Nothing runs without your approval. AI Pro helps you plan and build. The actual trading follows your rules inside a separate sub-account.

  • After launch, you stay in control. Pause, adjust, or revoke access from the Binance app.

Today, we're unveiling Binance AI Pro. Through a simple conversation, you can turn your trading ideas and strategies into tested, automated workflows.

Binance AI Pro is the latest addition to Binance Intelligence, our most ambitious lineup of AI products yet. Since August 2026, we've launched Agent OS, which lets developers build and connect agents to Binance’s capabilities and deep liquidity, and Binance AI, an assistant that personalizes the app experience for every user.

Start Building on Binance AI Pro

Say Your Idea in Plain Words

Start by describing your idea. AI Pro helps you plan, filling in the gaps and optimizing your logic, then visualizes the workflow on a canvas so you can see how the pieces fit together. Here are a few examples of what you can ask AI Pro to do:

  • Create a short daily report on how the market is doing

  • Set up a dollar-cost averaging plan (DCA) for Bitcoin

  • Suggest a conservative trading strategy for a $1,000 account

These are just a few examples. Binance AI Pro can be as simple or as advanced as you want it to be. 

Test it Before You Trust it

Before any real money is involved, you can see how your idea would have performed. Demo your strategy in practice mode with virtual money using historical data. Then tweak and refine until it does exactly what you want. 

Any workflow you build needs your explicit approval before it goes live. Binance AI Pro also runs its own checks on the coded workflow to confirm the logic executes without errors. This is purely a functionality check. It does not assess profitability, quality, or likely performance of your strategy. You will then choose where it operates: an existing sub-account, or a new one created for that strategy.

Everything You Need Is Already in Binance

Using AI in your trading shouldn't mean going back and forth between your trading screens and a handful of different AI chatbots.

Setting up Binance AI Pro doesn’t require a separate app or coding knowledge. The only thing you need is your Binance account. There’s also a range of leading AI models to choose from on the Premium Plan, including Claude and GPT frontier models, so you can build with what you already know. 

You Make the Final Decision

We’ve designed Binance AI Pro so that the person who built the strategy is always the one holding the controls. You decide what your AI can access, how much exposure it carries, and when it should stop. AI Pro follows the rules you set.

Every strategy you create runs within its own isolated sub-account, keeping activity contained and walled off from your main account. New workflows don't trade until you say so. If you change a workflow's logic, AI Pro creates a new version, and that version also needs your approval before it trades. 

After launch, you can pause, adjust or revoke access at any time.

  4. Review your strategy and test it with paper trading.

  5. Approve the strategy, then transfer funds to its dedicated sub-account to start live trading.

  2. Follow steps 3 to 5 above.

Final Thoughts

For years, the most powerful trading tools have sat behind closed doors. They were built for institutions, big banks, and trading firms, out of reach for everyday users. 

Binance AI Pro is the final piece of Binance Intelligence, a suite of products that put institutional-grade AI in the hands of every user.

  • Agent OS: build and connect AI agents with a dedicated toolkit.

  • Binance AI: a 24/7 assistant that adapts the Binance app to how you use it.

  • Binance AI Pro: turn your trading ideas into automated workflows.

The Rise of Programmable RWAs: From Tokenized Assets to On-Chain Utility

2026-10-16

Main Takeaways

  • Programmable RWAs are tokenized, on-chain real-world assets that can be lent, pooled and used as collateral.

  • On-chain RWA value is up 85.2% this year to $34.18B, but that’s still only about 0.01% of the markets it could reach. Past performance is not indicative of future results.

  • Binance Wallet is a self-custodial Web3 product, separate from Binance’s regulated exchange services, and one of many ways to explore programmable RWAs yourself.

*Note: Products and services mentioned here may not be available in your region. 

This article covers two separate things: research published by Binance Research, and information about Binance Wallet, a self-custodial Web3 product that gives users access to third-party Web3 protocols. Binance Wallet is not part of Binance's regulated exchange services. Using Binance Wallet is a separate choice from reading the research in this article.

RWA growth is broadening across major asset classes: bond and money-market funds drove 54.7% of this year’s on-chain AUM increase; equities another 22.4%. The more consequential shift lies in what happens once these assets are on-chain: whether they can be lent, pooled, or posted as collateral – that is, whether they are programmable. This blog examines what programmable RWAs are, the scale of their rise, and how to access them.

What are Programmable RWAs?

Programmable RWAs are real-world assets that have been tokenized and brought on-chain, with logic baked directly into their smart contracts. Rather than just representing an asset, they can enforce rules, automate payments, and serve as collateral or liquidity in on-chain markets. 

Explosive Growth, Room for Greater Penetration

Programmable RWAs are growing fast, and it’s still early days. One way to see how early is measuring Programmable Asset Ratio (PAR): the value of programmable on-chain assets as a share of the total market they could one day reach.

According to Binance Research, the markets tokenization could reach are worth more than $300 trillion. Just over $34 billion of that is on-chain today, a PAR of roughly 0.01%, which signals the market is growing quickly, and still has almost all of its potential ahead of it.

Equities and Bonds Lead the Way

Equities mirror this trend. Tokenized equities grew 390.4% this year to $4.43B, which is still only 0.0029% of the $151.9 trillion global listed-equity market. Meanwhile, their share of on-chain RWA value more than doubled from 4.9% to 13.0%.

Bonds and money-market funds are growing from a larger base. They hold $18.29B on-chain, with a PAR of about 0.0171%. That large pool of interest-bearing assets gives on-chain applications plenty to build on, while equities grow faster through wider distribution and easier access.

Room to Put Capital to Work

Utilization has plenty of room to grow too. Overall capital activation rate (CAR) is about 12%, so roughly $12 of every $100 in tokenized value is already being used in on-chain markets. The momentum is clear: equity CAR rose from 1.95% to 7.54% this year, and private credit has reached 49.67%. 

With so much tokenized capital still available to use, activation can keep growing without any new issuance. That makes the next opportunity twofold: bringing more assets on-chain, and giving holders more ways to use them across liquidity, lending and collateral markets.

A Separate Product: Binance Wallet

The research above comes from Binance Research and describes the broader programmable RWA market, independent of any specific Binance product. One option some users choose to explore programmable RWAs is Binance Wallet. 

Binance Wallet is a self-custodial Web3 product that gives users access to third-party Web3 protocols through its interface. It is operated separately from Binance's centralized exchange (CEX) and is not covered by the same regulatory status. You are solely responsible for your own custody, security, and compliance when using it.

How to Access Programmable RWAs

Binance Wallet gives you access to third-party protocols and dApps through its interface, but it is not the primary service provider for them, those services are operated independently.

1. Set up your Binance Wallet: The Binance Wallet is built into the Binance App. 

Open the app, go to [Wallet] > [Web3 Wallet] and tap [Create Wallet]. If you already have a wallet, you can import it instead.

2. Fund your wallet with a stablecoin: Stablecoins such as USDT and USDC hold a steady value and work with most token swaps, so they're a convenient starting point. 

Tap Receive in your wallet, then withdraw funds from your Binance Exchange account to your Binance Wallet, or fund it from another wallet address or with a credit or debit card. 

When the withdrawal or transfer is done, your stablecoin will show up under Assets. Note: You may need a gas token to perform the swap. Fund your wallet with a gas token the same way.

3. Open Binance Wallet’s trade tab: Use the wallet’s trade tab to access programmable RWAs such as tokenized stocks, ETFs, or other structured products.

4. Swap your stablecoin for a programmable RWA: Go to the Trade tab. Pick your preferred stablecoin to swap, enter how much of the programmable RWA you want to buy, and tap Approve & Swap. 

5. Store or use your programmable RWAs: Your tokens are now in your Binance Wallet, where you can hold them or use them on-chain.

Final Thoughts

Programmable RWAs turn tokenized real-world assets into ones you can use on-chain. With only about 0.01% of the markets they could reach tokenized so far, and about 12% of that capital already in use, there's plenty of room to grow. The shift from issuing assets to putting them to work is still in its early stages, and it’s one worth watching.

The next phase of growth likely depends on two things moving together: more assets coming on-chain, and more ways for holders to actually use what they already have. Equities and bonds are growing from different starting points, but both show the same pattern, low penetration, rising activation. That combination, rather than either number alone, is what signals where programmable RWAs go from here.

Understand Bonds With Binance Academy: From Lending to Fixed Income

Main Takeaways

  • Binance Academy’s new, free course, Understanding Bonds: From Lending to Fixed Income, explains how bonds work.

  • The course also covers how coupons, maturity, and yield work, why bond prices move inversely to interest rates, what credit ratings signal, and how bonds may fit into a balanced portfolio.

  • You don’t need any investing or finance background, and the course takes about 25-30 minutes across six modules in three sections.

The bond market is worth more than $100 trillion and sits at the center of global finance. Its core ideas of lending, interest and risk appear in every market, including crypto. But for many newcomers, the jargon alone (such as face value, coupon, yield, maturity) is enough to put them off. Binance Academy’s new free course, Understanding Bonds: From Lending to Fixed Income, cuts through that jargon and explains how bonds actually work.

Do You Need Prior Experience?

This course is designed with beginners in mind. Concepts are explained in plain language and build on each other step by step, focusing on ideas rather than the rules of any one country or platform, so it applies broadly. If you've already taken our Understanding Stocks: From Shares to Markets course, some ideas here may feel familiar.

Crypto users who already trade but have never studied traditional fixed-income markets may find it especially useful for connecting the two worlds. Interest rate expectations affect how willing people are to hold riskier assets, so the forces that move bonds can also shape crypto market sentiment. The mechanisms differ, but the lesson is the same: the price of money matters everywhere.

What You Will Learn

The course is divided into three sections and includes six modules. Each module is approximately four to five minutes, with a total course duration of around 25 to 30 minutes. By the end of the course, you'll be able to:

Understand What a Bond Is

A bond is a loan, and when you buy one, you’re the lender. The borrower owes you interest and has to pay back the full amount later. You'll learn the three basic terms every bond has: the amount borrowed (face value), the interest payments (coupon), and the repayment date (maturity). You'll also learn how owning a bond differs from owning stock. If a company runs into trouble, bondholders usually get paid before shareholders, but there's no direct upside when the company grows.

Learn Why Bonds Are Issued

Find out why governments and companies borrow by selling bonds instead of taking out bank loans or selling shares. You'll compare government and corporate bonds and see what the money pays for, such as roads, factories, or older debts. You'll also look at the key trade-offs. Borrowing has to be paid back with interest, but the owners keep full ownership. Selling shares brings in money with no repayment required, since investors receive a stake in the company instead.

Better Understand Coupons, Maturity, and Yield

Learn how a bond pays you and clear up one of the most common mix-ups in investing: coupon versus yield. The coupon is the fixed interest set when the bond is first sold. Maturity is the date you get your original money back. Yield is your actual return, based on the price you paid. If you pay less for the same interest payments, your return goes up.

Learn How Bond Prices and Risks Work

Explore the relationship between bond prices and interest rates. A simple seesaw example shows why an older bond paying 5% loses value once new bonds pay 7%. You'll also learn about the main types of bonds, including government, corporate, and high-yield bonds. You'll find out what credit ratings mean, understand the three real risks bonds carry (interest rate, credit, and inflation), and see how bonds can fit in a diversified portfolio.

Final Thoughts

While bonds aren’t crypto-native assets, the ideas behind them, such as lending, interest and risk, shape every market, crypto included. Real understanding comes from a clear picture of what a bond is, how the bond market behaves and where the risks lie. That's exactly what Understanding Bonds: From Lending to Fixed Income is built to cover.

  • Usage is concentrated outside the traditional session. In August 2026, only 42% of bStocks volume occurred during regular U.S. market hours, and on-chain usage indicators suggest tokenized securities are being used beyond 24/7 trading.

It's official: bStocks has crossed the $1B milestone, four months after launching in June. We see this as a strong signal that users want crypto-native TradFi exposure. Looking at the broader market, tokenized equities are the fastest growing real-world asset (RWA) of 2026, up 390.4% in market cap year-to-date, according to Binance Research. bStocks alone represents roughly a quarter of the sector’s market capitalization, as of October 2026.

Why bStocks is Leading the Charge

The tokenized equity sector has experienced massive growth since June, and we don't believe it's a coincidence that bStocks launched around the same time. 

If you're new to bStocks, they're tokenized securities that give users 1:1 exposure to selected stocks and ETFs. You can learn more in our introductory blog post. Below, we break down the numbers and the product features behind the growth of bStocks.

1:1 conversion with no fees

bStocks holders can convert between their token and the corresponding stocks on Binance at a 1:1 rate with no conversion fees. Some platforms don't have a conversion mechanism, forcing users to make two separate trades – sell the token and rebuy the stock directly – if they want to switch.

Binance users can hold bStocks when they want to trade outside regular hours, withdraw them to a self-custody wallet, or use them on-chain. When they’d rather hold the stock directly, they can convert anytime with no fees, and vice versa. So far, users have converted more than $6B between the two formats, as of October 2026, more than six times the AUM itself.

Trading outside the bell

bStocks operate around the clock, including weekends, with the majority of trading activity taking place outside the regular session. According to Binance Research data from August 2026, only 42% of bStocks volume happens during regular U.S. market hours, compared with 89.2% for conventional U.S. equities. The other 58% was well distributed across pre-market, post-market, overnight, and weekend sessions.

Regular sessions capture the bulk of conventional U.S. equity volume, but earnings reports, policy announcements, and major headlines often land after the market closes. Instead of waiting for the next session, bStocks holders can adjust their positions as those events happen.

Built to be used on-chain

Once in an external wallet, bStocks can be deployed across on-chain applications. bStocks utilization has reached 11.2%, about 3.8 percentage points above the rate for tokenized equities overall, according to Binance Research. 

Based on Binance Research’s analysis of on-chain activity, outstanding borrowing against bStocks rose from 5.5% of deposited collateral at the end of June to 46.2% by September 10, 2026, with approximately $3.1 million borrowed against $6.8 million of collateral. 

On-chain transfers of tokenized stocks, including trading volume, exceeded $100 billion in Q3 2026, more than 16 times the $6 billion recorded in Q1. bStocks drove much of the surge, accounting for over 90% of weekly transfer volume at its early-August peak, per Binance Research.

One account for all finance

For many Binance users, bStocks is just one product of a wider suite that includes perpetuals, options, direct stocks, and crypto. In fact, according to Binance Research, 58.5% of early bStocks users had already traded perpetual futures, direct equities, or both as of August 2026, before they bought their first bStock.

Growing coverage

We've steadily increased coverage to meet the growing demand. When we first launched bStocks in June, there were only five tickers available. Four months later, bStocks now covers nearly 100 tickers across a variety of sectors, including AI infrastructure, semiconductors, sector ETFs, and more.

Final Thoughts

The $1B AUM milestone is just a snapshot of the broader momentum we're seeing. That headline number is still early by global benchmarks, part of a rapidly growing market that is opening new pathways into traditional finance. We are seeing the majority of bStocks trading taking place outside regular U.S. market hours, users converting billions between bStocks and direct stocks, and increasing utility that goes beyond the ability to trade 24/7.

Only 0.0025% of the global stock market is on-chain today, and even sub-1% penetration by 2030 would represent significant growth, with Binance Research base-case estimates at $349 billion.

Crypto Market Performance in September 2026

In September, total crypto market capitalization rose 11.0% to $2.99T, despite a challenging macro and policy backdrop.

August inflation held at 3.4% and payrolls beat expectations. On September 16, the Fed raised rates 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00%, its first hike since July 2023, and 16 of 18 officials expect another by year-end.

The CLARITY Act stalled after a 49-50 cloture vote, though the CFTC and SEC moved crypto rules forward on September 18.

BTC still rallied. Spot ETFs drew $3.49B, turning 2026 flows positive, and Strategy bought 2,615 BTC. This made it the strongest of four straight positive Septembers.

Majors were broadly positive in September, with gains driven by ETF flows, institutional partnerships, and network catalysts.

ZEC led with 65.9%, reaching a market capitalization of roughly $24B as shielded pools neared record levels. LINK rose 26.7% after Circle launched Arc mainnet with Chainlink as its foundational oracle. SOL gained 19.1% as spot SOL ETFs posted their best week since launch and Solana stablecoins hit a record $17.3B. DOGE added 16.2% alongside the broader rally.

BNB rose 12.7%, and BNB Chain became the only chain holding $1B in tokenized stocks. ETH added 10.8% on $689.9M of weekly spot ETF inflows. HYPE was the weakest, up 4.3%, as its August rally cooled despite an all-time high on September 19.

Binance Pay Expands Agentic Payments Into Real-World Commerce

2026-10-13

Main Takeaways

  • Binance Pay brings agentic payments into real-world commerce, letting AI agents and applications complete real transactions, starting with AI-powered hotel bookings.

  • It supports payments from self-custody wallets with no card details and no gas management, with settlement on BNB Chain.

  • Travelers can book from over 2.2 million accommodations via Travala’s AI travel agent, with up to 10% cashback in BNB and AVA on a first qualifying booking.

Until now, onchain payments have shared one assumption: a human is present at the moment of payment. AI agents can already search, compare, and find the right option, but they’ve always needed a human to open a wallet and confirm before anything can be paid for. 

Binance x402 closes that gap. You authorize the payment in advance, and your agent completes the transaction without needing you to confirm again in the moment. That’s the problem Binance Pay set out to solve with Binance x402, the payment infrastructure for agents, APIs, and digital services introduced earlier this year. Now, that work is reaching real-world commerce, starting with booking a hotel through an AI agent.

Bringing Agentic Payments to Hotel Bookings

Binance Pay has teamed up with BNB Chain and Travala to enable AI-powered hotel bookings using USDT on BNB Smart Chain. Travelers authorize payment from a self-custody wallet in advance, then search, choose, and book directly through Travala's AI travel agent, with Binance Pay handling execution and settlement: no card details, gas management, or currency conversion required. 

In this collaboration, BNB Chain provides the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) SDK and agentic framework, and Binance Pay provides the payment settlement infrastructure. The launch is part of Binance Pay’s broader work on Agent Pay, which is building payment infrastructure for AI agents, applications and machine-driven commerce.

Get Up to 10% Back on Your First AI Agent Hotel Booking

Booking through an AI agent works a little differently from a standard checkout. You authorize payment in advance, so your agent can complete the booking without you confirming again at the moment of payment.

Authorize: Approve payment in advance using USDT from a BNB Smart Chain wallet.

Search: Tell Travala’s AI agent where and when you want to travel.

Choose: Select your preferred accommodation from Travala’s inventory presented by the AI agent.

Book: The agent completes payment and your booking is confirmed.

It all happens directly in the browser, with no set up required, no card information to enter, and no gas fees to manage. Hotel bookings are available at launch, with additional travel products expected to be supported in the future. 

To mark the launch, eligible travelers can receive 7% cashback in BNB on their first qualifying hotel booking through Travala’s AI travel agent. Eligible AVA Smart members can receive an additional 3% cashback in AVA. The promotion applies to qualifying bookings of at least US$400, subject to applicable eligibility requirements and promotion terms.

How Binance Pay Powers the Settlement

The biggest change with agent payments isn’t simply paying with crypto. It’s who has to manage the payment process.

Standard crypto booking 

Agent booking via Binance x402

User searches for a hotel

User tells the agent what they want

User selects the hotel

Agent finds and presents suitable options

User enters checkout

User selects the preferred option

User connects a wallet

User gives one payment authorization

User checks token balance

Agent handles the payment flow

User makes sure they have the right asset

Binance Pay executes the transaction

User checks whether they have enough gas

Binance Pay covers network gas

User reviews the transaction details

Payment parameters are handled in the background

User signs and broadcasts the transaction

Settlement is executed automatically

User waits for onchain confirmation

Payment confirmation is returned automatically

User returns to complete the booking

Agent completes the booking end-to-end

The user chooses and authorizes. The agent and Binance Pay handle execution, settlement and confirmation behind the scenes. Here’s what that looks like technically. 

When a traveler confirms a booking, they sign an EIP-712 Permit2 authorization offchain. The MPP SDK verifies the signature, wallet balance, allowance, and payment parameters, then sends the verified payment instruction to Binance Pay. 

Binance Pay then broadcasts the transaction and pays the required network gas. Funds move from the user's wallet to Travala. Once settlement is complete, MPP marks the payment as successful and issues an onchain receipt confirming the transaction.

The Travala launch is one example of a broader shift in how payments may work as AI agents become more capable. Binance Pay is building toward a world where payments can become a native capability for AI applications, connecting agents with APIs, digital services, merchants and real-world commerce. 

Different use cases may rely on different protocols and agent frameworks, but the underlying requirement remains the same: AI agents need a reliable way to turn an authorized action into a completed payment. Binance Pay aims to provide that payment layer.

Binance Pay is the payment service within the Binance ecosystem that enables eligible users to make and receive payments through supported payment experiences, with user-verification, risk-management, transaction-monitoring, and account-security controls built in. Agent Pay extends that same infrastructure to AI agents acting on a user’s behalf.

This is the shift Binance Pay is enabling: from users managing crypto transactions themselves to AI agents using crypto as a seamless payment rail to complete real tasks. The Travala hotel booking is the first example, with more travel products and use cases to follow.

  • Institutional capital is pouring into digital assets, with 86% of institutional investors holding or planning allocations in 2025, but almost all of it goes into passive products.

  • The gap isn’t unique to crypto. Capital raising everywhere favors size over performance, but crypto has no standardized way to discover or compare active managers at all.

  • Capital Connect closes that gap: an exchange-native marketplace to browse, evaluate, and allocate to active strategies, with verified data and zero platform fee.

Note: This is a general announcement. Certain products and services may not be available in your region. Terms and conditions apply. 

By 2025, 86% of institutional investors held or developed plans to allocate to digital assets, and 83% had committed to increasing their holdings, according to the EY-Parthenon 2025 Institutional Investor Digital Assets Survey. Capital is flowing in.

But almost all of it is going into passive products. The same EY survey found that 81% of institutional investors prefer spot exposure through a registered vehicle like an ETF. That solves for passive and beta exposure, but there is no equivalent on-ramp for active crypto portfolio managers. Dedicated crypto hedge fund AUM is only $10 to $15 billion despite the broader institutional wave, according to the Crypto Insights Group's 2025 Industry Guide.

Two-thirds of institutional investors allocate to digital assets, but over one-third keep exposure below 2%, and 41% said they would increase exposure if operational and compliance risks were reduced, as per the 7th Annual Global Crypto Hedge Fund Report.

This is not a demand problem. It’s an infrastructure problem. And it’s exactly what Binance Capital Connect was built to address.

The Problem Is Older Than Crypto: Top Managers Get 80% of Capital

Capital raising in traditional finance is already relationship-driven and top-heavy. Over 85% of institutional investors source new manager relationships through personal networks or prime broker capital introduction desks, per AIMA research on emerging manager capital raising. Discovery

Over 85% of institutional investors source new managers through personal networks or prime brokers, per AIMA. In crypto, there is no equivalent. Investors have no centralized marketplace to browse, compare, and evaluate strategies on standardized metrics.

Diligence

There is no standardized performance data or benchmarking framework across crypto fund managers. Investors can’t compare NAV, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, or gross vs net returns on equal footing.

Distribution

Emerging managers outperform larger ones by nearly 2x, per IG Prime, yet they can’t raise capital. In crypto, no institutional channel exists for independent trading teams to reach verified investors.

Capital Connect is an open, exchange-native strategy marketplace on Binance that connects verified and eligible institutional investors with independent trading teams. It covers active strategies across digital and traditional assets, with full performance transparency and zero platform fee.

Investors browse multiple trading teams and strategy types in one place, with Binance-verified performance data displayed side by side: NAV, Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, max drawdown, and gross vs net returns. No Telegram groups, no conference matchmaking, no third-party platforms to navigate. 

When the market changes, investors can switch strategies on the same platform. For trading teams, Capital Connect provides access to a verified institutional investor base already embedded in the Binance ecosystem.

  3. Invest: Allocate with zero platform fee

The institutional wave into digital assets isn’t slowing down. It’s accelerating. But without infrastructure for active strategy allocation, capital will continue to flow into passive products by default, and the managers best positioned to generate alpha will continue to struggle for capital.

The managers who outperform shouldn’t be the ones struggling to raise. Closing that gap takes more than another fund or partnership. It takes a marketplace built to make performance visible and capital movable. Performance should be the thing that raises capital, not proximity to it. Capital Connect makes that possible.

Why Binance Created The Blockchain 100

The Blockchain 100 was established to recognize creators who contribute to public understanding of blockchain technology, digital assets, and financial markets, from established industry voices to emerging creators working across different areas of crypto and financial education.

That work takes many forms. Independent researchers analyze blockchain developments, educators introduce newcomers to crypto fundamentals, and community leaders facilitate discussions and share knowledge with their audiences.

The Blockchain 100 extends beyond the annual awards ceremony through a year-round video interview series featuring voices from across the crypto industry. The interviews give guests an opportunity to discuss their work, share personal experiences, and address developments shaping the space.

Building on its inaugural edition, The Blockchain 100 returns in 2026 with an expanded scope that includes creators from both cryptocurrency and traditional finance.

With its second edition approaching, The Blockchain 100 continues to recognize the creators helping audiences better understand crypto and financial markets. 2026-08-21

Main Takeaways

  • For three decades, participating in financial markets has involved clicking a screen. That assumption is starting to break down as AI software begins acting on our behalf.

  • Open standards like MCP are making it easier for AI applications to discover and call external tools, which is speeding up agent integrations into daily life.

  • Binance Agent OS helps developers connect AI agents to Binance trading, market data, wallets, payments, and on-chain capabilities, with permissions and access controls that can be set and revoked at any time.

Binance began as a crypto exchange. From there, we built a financial super app, unifying crypto, traditional finance, tokenized securities, cross-border payments, and social features into a single ecosystem.

Now we’re focused on bringing AI agents into Binance’s financial super app experience with Binance Agent OS, a bridge that connects our core capabilities to a new generation of software.

Why Crypto Is a Natural Fit for Agentic Finance

AI agents are software-native. The tasks they perform involve frequent, conditional decisions — patterns that don’t map cleanly onto legacy financial systems designed around rigid business hours, middlemen, and multi-day settlement cycles.

As agents evolve and take on more complex tasks, they’ll need fast payment rails that can keep pace. Traditional billing is too much friction for an agent trying to pay for a single API call or a slice of compute power. Stablecoins and crypto networks, by contrast, can support real-time settlement and global transferability. Agents also cannot open or operate a traditional bank account, but it can hold a wallet. That makes agent-to-agent payments possible, within boundaries set by their users. 

Building a Financial Capability Layer

The first wave of consumer AI products helped people find and interpret information. AI agents go a step further by interpreting and executing without needing a prompt at every step.

Three things have fallen into place at once. 

First, agents have settled on a common language: the Model Context Protocol (MCP), open-sourced by Anthropic in late 2024 and since adopted by OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and AWS. It has become the de facto way AI applications discover and call external tools. Public MCP servers grew from roughly 2,000 at the start of 2025 to more than 10,000 by year-end.

Second, the environments where agents run have continued to scale. Cursor – an AI-native code editor – climbed from about $150M in annualized revenue in early 2025 to roughly $2B a year later, and GitHub Copilot passed 20 million cumulative users. 

Third, capital is following the pattern. Analysts project the agent market growing from single-digit billions in 2025 to between $24B and $53B by 2030, based on 2025–26 market size estimates from Grand View, Omdia, MarketsandMarkets, MarkNtel, and Precedence.

Why Binance’s Infrastructure Matters

But even the smartest model is constrained by what it plugs into. An agent that trades well is still limited by the trading engine it routes through, and an agent capable of market analysis is only as effective as the quality of the data it consumes. MCP is, put simply, a convenient gateway; what matters more is the infrastructure standing behind it.

With a global user base of over 300 million and high-throughput infrastructure backed by security and risk controls that have been battle-tested for nearly a decade, Binance is designed to support agentic workflows that require live data, fast routing, and reliable execution. 

Opening the Super App to AI Agents

Binance Agent OS gives developers a dedicated toolkit to connect agents into deep trading liquidity and a broader set of markets beyond crypto for eligible users, including over 7,000 U.S.-listed stocks, TradFi perpetual contracts, and tokenized securities through bStocks.

Beyond trading, Agent OS extends to payments, wallets, and on-chain activity — including machine-to-machine settlement over x402, wallet transactions, and DeFi access through Binance Web3 APIs, as well as a curated library of skills.

Security controls are granular. Users decide which features each agent can access, and every agent operates from a dedicated sub-account that keeps funds in the main account separate. Individual agents can be disconnected at any time, and an emergency killswitch revokes access to all agents at once. Execution is handled by software – rather than taps on a screen – but the user still sets the boundaries it works within.

Final Thoughts

How we interact with financial services is changing: from juggling multiple apps, to unified super apps, to experiences where users set goals and delegate AI agents to carry out the steps. Binance’s role is to provide the tools needed to build that experience responsibly. To learn more about Binance Agent OS, read our launch blog post or get started on the official Agent OS page.

First, agents have settled on a common language: the Model Context Protocol (MCP), open-sourced by Anthropic in late 2024 and since adopted by OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and AWS. It has become the de facto way AI applications discover and call external tools. Public MCP servers grew from roughly 2,000 at the start of 2025 to more than 10,000 by year-end.

Second, the environments where agents run have continued to scale. Cursor – an AI-native code editor – climbed from about $150M in annualized revenue in early 2025 to roughly $2B a year later, and GitHub Copilot passed 20 million cumulative users. 

Third, capital is following the pattern. Analysts project the agent market growing from single-digit billions in 2025 to between $24B and $53B by 2030, based on 2025–26 market size estimates from Grand View, Omdia, MarketsandMarkets, MarkNtel, and Precedence.

Why Binance’s Infrastructure Matters

But even the smartest model is constrained by what it plugs into. An agent that trades well is still limited by the trading engine it routes through, and an agent capable of market analysis is only as effective as the quality of the data it consumes. MCP is, put simply, a convenient gateway; what matters more is the infrastructure standing behind it.

With a global user base of over 300 million and high-throughput infrastructure backed by security and risk controls that have been battle-tested for nearly a decade, Binance is designed to support agentic workflows that require live data, fast routing, and reliable execution. 

Opening the Super App to AI Agents

Binance Agent OS gives developers a dedicated toolkit to connect agents into deep trading liquidity and a broader set of markets beyond crypto for eligible users, including over 7,000 U.S.-listed stocks, TradFi perpetual contracts, and tokenized securities through bStocks.

Beyond trading, Agent OS extends to payments, wallets, and on-chain activity — including machine-to-machine settlement over x402, wallet transactions, and DeFi access through Binance Web3 APIs, as well as a curated library of skills.

Security controls are granular. Users decide which features each agent can access, and every agent operates from a dedicated sub-account that keeps funds in the main account separate. Individual agents can be disconnected at any time, and an emergency killswitch revokes access to all agents at once. Execution is handled by software – rather than taps on a screen – but the user still sets the boundaries it works within.

Final Thoughts

How we interact with financial services is changing: from juggling multiple apps, to unified super apps, to experiences where users set goals and delegate AI agents to carry out the steps. Binance’s role is to provide the tools needed to build that experience responsibly. To learn more about Binance Agent OS, read our launch blog post or get started on the official Agent OS page.

What is Binance Agent OS?

Binance Agent OS is a gateway and toolkit for connecting AI agents to Binance. Our built-in MCP server currently supports trading and market data access, with payment and on-chain capabilities coming in future releases. How to Connect Your AI Agent in Minutes

Connect your AI agent to Binance by adding the Binance MCP server to your agent environment, then authenticate it from your Binance account. 

For Claude Code users:

  1. Add the MCP server. Open your terminal, then copy and paste the following command:

    claude mcp add binance-mcp-server --transport http https://agent.binance.com/mcp/agentic

  2. Open your agent environment and enter /mcp. This lists your connected MCP servers, including binance-mcp-server.

  3. Start authentication. Select binance-mcp-server and press Enter, then choose [Authenticate]. Your browser will redirect to an authentication page.

  4. Select your agent. From the dropdown, choose which agent you want to connect to Binance.

  5. Set permissions. Toggle which features and products this agent can access. Anything left off stays inaccessible until you enable it.

Return to your agent environment to configure trading parameters. You can review or change these permissions at any time under [Sub Accounts] → [Account Management]. 

Binance Agent OS works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, ChatGPT, and self-built agents. Setup guides for other environments are available at binance.com/agent-os.

Available capabilities on Binance Agent OS depend on the connection method. MCP currently covers trading and market data access, while developers can use other Agent OS integrations for payments and on-chain activity until these are added to MCP.

Account

Binance trading analysis tools

Inside the Numbers Behind Binance’s Financial Super App

2026-08-06

Main Takeaways

  • Binance is building a single, always-on account for direct stocks, tokenized securities, and TradFi perps, giving people access traditional finance has never offered them.

  • bStocks added $565.9 million in tokenized equity value in seven weeks, outpacing every comparable product. 

  • Across the seven weekends since launch, bStocks priced in a median 92% of Monday’s stock moves before the market even opened.

  • Binance’s Co-CEO, Yi He, first laid out that vision on stage at the Hong Kong Web3 Festival, a moment now captured in the short film 36 Hours With Yi.

Stock markets close for the weekend. bStocks don’t. 

They’re tokenized versions of U.S.-listed stocks that trade on Binance around the clock, convertible 1:1 with the underlying share whenever a user wants and with no conversion fees. 

Since launching on June 11, that always-on design has translated into real activity. By the end of July, bStocks had grown faster in absolute terms than any other major tokenized-security product — as tracked by TokenTerminal — adding over $565.9 million in outstanding supply, a +5,000% increase. Few tokenized products reach that kind of scale within their second month. 

While Wall Street Sleeps, bStocks Anticipate the Price

Growth tells you people are using the product. It doesn’t tell you whether the market trusts the price enough to act on it. Binance Research’s latest look at bStocks provides valuable insight into this question.

Compared against the other large issuers, bStocks at one point accounted for 27% of global tokenized equity market capitalization. Weekend trading on bStocks priced in a median 92% of the following Monday’s price gap in the underlying stock, and for gaps larger than 3%, bStocks called the direction correctly in all 41 instances observed since launch. 

In other words, while Wall Street is shut for the weekend, data indicates that bStocks is already pricing in Monday’s move, on BNB Chain, now the largest venue for on-chain equities. That trust has built fast: bStocks crossed $500 million in AUM less than seven weeks after launch.

That kind of growth doesn’t happen by accident. This year, Binance set a new target for its team that carried real weight. The goal was no longer one billion users, but three billion — a response to a specific, well-documented gap.

The Case for Three Billion

None of that trading activity matters much without the reason behind it. According to the World Bank, 1.3 billion adults remain unbanked worldwide. The barrier isn’t technology: 42% of unbanked adults already own a smartphone, a figure that rises above 50% in most regions outside South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa.

Equity markets tell an even starker version of the same story. Binance Research estimates that roughly 700 million people worldwide hold a brokerage account, meaning close to 89% of the global population has lacked meaningful access to U.S. equities, the single largest pool of investable wealth on the planet. 

That’s the gap Binance is built to close, at a scale few platforms can match. Binance already serves users across more than 100 countries. A traditional bank needs a branch, a deposit, and paperwork. A mobile-first platform just needs the phone people already have. That’s the logic behind Binance’s 3 billion target: digital financial access can reach people faster than traditional banking infrastructure ever will, because the device is already in their pocket.

One Account, No Closing Bell

Access starts with a phone, but delivering on it takes real scale. At the time of writing, DeFiLlama data show that Binance holds roughly $117 billion in reserve assets (excluding exchange-native tokens), about 5.5 times the level of the second-ranked exchange. 

Binance also commands around 30% of global crypto spot trading volume across centralized exchanges. It’s the world’s largest cryptocurrency platform by both user count and trading volume. TradFi builds directly on that foundation.

Most financial infrastructure was built around fixed hours and separate accounts. A typical brokerage is open roughly 32.5 hours a week, and stocks, options, and futures usually live in different accounts entirely. 

Binance runs 168 hours a week. One account carries a user through direct stocks, tokenized securities, and perpetual futures on ETFs and commodities, without waiting for a market somewhere else to open. 

This is the practical shape of Binance’s financial super app vision: a single, always-on place where trading, payments, and on-chain access sit together instead of being scattered across separate platforms.

TradFi in More Hands

An always-open account only matters if the people who need it can reach it. Look at who’s using bStocks and Direct Stocks, and it becomes clear that they can. More than 90% of these users come from emerging markets, and Gen Z makes up nearly 44% of Binance’s equity users, the largest single age group on the platform. 

For many of them, tokenized securities are the first brokerage access they’ve ever had. Opening an overseas account, wiring money internationally, and converting currency have long been the invisible tax on investing from outside a handful of major markets, one most people never think about because they’ve never had to pay it. Binance removes each of those steps, and the users turning up are the ones that friction used to price out entirely.

The pattern isn’t limited to bStocks, either. TradFi perpetuals on Binance now hold a 74% share of the global ETF perp market, up from 18% when the category launched in March, across a lineup that’s grown to 146 pairs. Different product, same shift: wherever Binance opens up a new corner of TradFi, the same underserved group of users is the first to walk through it.

The Moment This Started

Every number in this piece backs up something said out loud months earlier. At the Hong Kong Web3 Festival in April, Yi He, Binance Co-CEO, joined a fireside chat and put the words behind this vision on the record for the first time, months before any of the above existed.

“This year, I'm telling the team that we should aim for three billion,” she said. “To become a company with three billion users, it means Binance is not just a crypto exchange, but the world’s global financial infrastructure.” The moment is captured in 36 Hours With Yi, a short behind-the-scenes look at her time in Hong Kong, out now.

From that fireside chat to a finished film took months of production; bStocks took only seven weeks to cross $500 million. The products moved faster than the film did, and that’s the story worth considering here – everything that’s happened since that one line on stage.

Final Thoughts

1.3 billion people are still without a bank account. Nine in ten people worldwide still lack meaningful access to global equities. That’s the scale of what three billion users is meant to solve. Four months on from that fireside chat in Hong Kong, the direction has stopped being just a line from a stage. It’s a pattern showing up across every product Binance has built since.

One Account, Every Market: How Binance is Building a Multi-Asset Super App

2026-06-12

This is a general educational announcement and should not be construed as solicitation to conduct any actions. Products mentioned may not be available in your jurisdiction. 

Main Takeaways

  • 7,000+ U.S. stocks and ETFs now trade alongside crypto in one Binance app and account, on a 24/5 schedule, with tokenized securities just added to the platform

  • Stock trades on Binance settle in stablecoins (USDC, USDT, USD1, $U) or BNB, reducing friction in both user experience and market access for billions of unbanked users globally. 

  • Direct stocks and ETFs, as well as the new tokenized securities functionality, mark a significant step for Binance as a financial super app, expanding from crypto trading to multi-asset trading on blockchain rails.

Every app starts as one thing. Amazon sold books before it sold everything. Grab started with rides, then grew into a payments staple across Southeast Asia.

When Binance launched in 2017, half the battle of getting into crypto was navigating the interfaces. Legacy exchanges at the time were slow, cluttered, and built for tech-savvy users. Binance focused on the basics that traders cared about: deep liquidity, faster execution, straightforward onboarding, and an accessible user experience.

Since then, we’ve continued expanding what users can access on Binance, from more trading pairs to an entire universe of products spanning payments, social, chat, and earning. Crypto remains at the center of Binance's identity. Adding stocks now establishes Binance as a complete gateway to the wider financial system. 

With Binance, you can now buy and sell over 7,000 U.S. stocks and ETFs settled in stablecoins in select jurisdictions, right alongside your crypto, in a single app.

Crypto, Stocks, and ETFs on Binance

For the last nine years, Binance has been building toward a financial system that’s more efficient, more accessible, and with fewer barriers. A core part of that vision has been creating a platform where users have greater command over their financial lives.

Over 7,000 U.S. stocks and ETFs now sit alongside crypto within one Binance app and account. Stock trading is available on an extended 24/5 schedule, because everyone should have the ability to react to market-moving news as they happen.

Alongside direct stock trading, we also launched bStocks, a tokenized securities product offering on-chain access to select U.S. stocks. With bStocks, users can trade their positions 24/7, take them off platform into their own wallets, and deploy them into DApps.

Direct stock trading and bStocks play an integral role in our super app vision, bringing crypto, equities, and on-chain finance into a unified user experience. For more details on bStocks, you can read our full announcement post. 

Removing the Friction of Multi-Asset Portfolios 

The concept of diversified investing continues to expand, spanning across multiple asset classes. Today’s investors hold crypto, equities, ETFs, and stablecoins, and they want flexibility to move between them.

On Binance, the multi-asset experience has been simplified to a few taps. Users can go from Bitcoin to widely followed U.S. equities without switching platforms.

Reducing friction also goes beyond menus and interfaces. Billions of people have a phone and an internet connection, but limited access to traditional bank infrastructure. Because stock trades settle in stablecoins on Binance, even people who previously lacked access can now trade U.S. stocks on crypto-native rails. In the first week alone, over 80% of direct stock trading volume on Binance came from emerging-market users, showing how quickly demand surfaces when friction is reduced.

Stock trading on Binance marks the first time when people from eligible jurisdictions around the world can buy and sell U.S. stocks using stablecoins in a regulated manner.

Final Thoughts

Binance started with crypto, and crypto will remain our foundation. It is still the most open, programmable, and global financial rail available today. Everything we build is guided by our core mission of advancing equitable financial access and building a more transparent and safe system for all.

Bringing stocks and ETFs into the Binance ecosystem reflects what we’ve been doing since the beginning: give users the tools they need to control their own financial futures, whether it’s through 24/5 access to stablecoin-denominated U.S. stock trading pairs or the flexibility to trade across multiple asset classes on one simple interface trusted by over 300 million users.

5 Reasons Not to Join Binance

2026-01-30

Main Takeaways

  • Working at Binance isn’t for everyone. This article is an honest take on what it feels like to work in a high-bar, high-tempo environment built around our five core values. 

  • Our values show up in our work daily: protecting users, reducing friction, staying fast and autonomous, taking direct feedback, and collaborating globally without bloated meetings.

  • If this pace energizes you, read on to understand how we work and what we expect, then explore open roles on our careers page.

If you’re looking for a predictable routine, comfortable certainty, and a job that stays neatly inside the lines, this is your sign to close the tab. Binance is a high-performance, results-driven place where ownership is real and execution speed matters. While it may appeal to some, it may be the deal-breaker for others.

Still here? Below are five reasons you might not want to join Binance, each tied to a core value – and each a feature if you are the kind of builder who thrives here. For a quick peek, hit play on our culture video below to see it in motion.

Freedom: Not Your Typical 9-5

Since Binance is global and remote-first, adapting time zones are part of the job. If you love neat calendars, predictable hours, and everyone online at the same time, this will test your patience and your planning skills.

But here’s the fun part: “Freedom” at Binance is real. You’re trusted to manage your schedule and your output, which means you can build a rhythm that actually fits your life. Some days run long, some hours are weird, and sometimes, that’s exactly what makes it great.

If you are a night owl, you can build your rhythm around it. If you want to hit the gym at 2pm and enjoy an empty pilates class, go for it. When you see a cheap flight home on a Monday instead of a Sunday, take it. The point isn’t “always on,” it’s high trust: you own your time, your outcomes, and your impact. 

If you want rigid structure handed to you, this will feel chaotic. If you want autonomy and can handle the accountability that comes with it, it’s hard to beat.

Humility: Feedback is Part of the Job

At Binance, you’re trusted to take ownership and make calls without someone hovering over your shoulder. The catch is you’re also seriously accountable. From the outside, that can look intense: you’ll own complex work, escalate messy issues, coordinate decisions across teams, and stay open to feedback even when it’s a little humbling.

If you need feedback to be gentle, indirect, or wrapped in a compliment sandwich, you’ll struggle. Sometimes you’ll get a message that basically says, “Not good enough yet.” Sometimes someone more junior will spot your mistake, in a group chat, with receipts. If your default mode is defensiveness, Binance will be a frustrating place to be.

Humility here is practical: take a breath, say “good catch,” fix it, and ship the better version. You don’t point fingers or blame the process, or treat disagreement like drama.

While it can be uncomfortable, it can also be a turning point. You can get better fast when you stop spending energy protecting your pride and start spending it to improve the work at hand.

Collaboration: Less Hierarchy, More Momentum

Binance isn’t a top-down place where decisions wait politely for titles to weigh in. Teams are empowered, adaptable, and expected to move fast. So if you rely on strict chains of command, or you’re used to alignment coming from seniority rather than results, our flat hierarchy will feel unfamiliar.

Collaboration here is straightforward: shared goals, honest communication, and a bias toward action, often asynchronous. Speed at this scale comes from being direct, making clear inquiries, giving the right context, and pulling in the right people at the right moment.

In practice, it looks like this: you ask, provide context, and follow up fast until it’s resolved. Instead of dragging half the organization into a meeting to “align,” you’re expected to write things down, make decisions visible, and move the work forward in a way others can build on. In an asynchronous environment, trust is built through follow-through. Even if you have never met a teammate in person, you’ll feel the strength of collaboration when the work ships and the outcome is clear.

If you love structure for structure’s sake, you’ll feel friction. If you love sharp teammates who move quickly and stay focused on the team outcome, you’ll thrive. Of course, when teams are empowered to move, the pace gets real, fast.

Hardcore: Build While You Run

Crypto never sleeps. That means you’re always learning, iterating quickly, and getting comfortable with a little uncertainty. Our “Hardcore” value is about resilience, urgency, and building with focus in a fast-moving environment.

If your ideal workday requires perfect clarity before you start, this won’t feel like a fit. There are moments when the right answer isn’t obvious, the situation is evolving in real time, with the expectation to run. You build a playbook while you’re running it. Amid ambiguity, you make the call, test it, iterate fast.

Day to day, “Hardcore” looks like this: you pick the highest-impact problem and get moving. You ship the first useful version, then improve it fast. You work hard, stay curious, and keep your energy pointed at outcomes. When something doesn’t land, you don’t spiral or stall. You learn fast, fix what broke, and get back up with a better approach.

The upside is that when you deliver, people notice. You need a growth mindset that can take the pressure, learn quickly, and keep momentum when things are moving fast and not fully defined.

The reason we push this hard is that the end game is always the user. 

User-Focused: Our North Star

If you’re not excited about building things that are genuinely useful for users, this probably isn’t your playground. At Binance, when your work goes live, real people use what you ship, every day, at scale.

Being “User-Focused” is the job. You’ll obsess over edge cases because users shouldn’t pay for our assumptions. You’ll rewrite a copy until it’s crystal clear because clarity protects people. You’ll fight to remove friction because users’ time matters. And you’ll take pride in the invisible work, the safeguards, improvements, and fixes that keep users secure and their trust intact.

If you’re chasing recognition more than outcomes, you might miss the point, because satisfying users is our end game. But if you love making things smoother, safer, and more reliable for users, you’ll fit right in.

Final Thoughts: Binance is Not for Everyone

Binance’s vision is to increase the freedom of money globally, and we don’t take that lightly. This culture is built for people who have high standards, real ownership, and work that ships into the real world.

Here’s the last reality check: if you’re after comfort, predictability, and low-stakes days, you’ll probably be happier elsewhere. But if you want a role that stretches you, trusts you, and keeps you interested because the impact is real, you might have found your place.

Comfort seekers, skip this. Builders, come exchange the world. Explore open roles at binance.com/careers now!
